Repo: /opt/nxeon (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma, production customer dashboard). Work in an isolated git worktree — `git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wip-hosting-redesign -b feature/hosting-overview-redesign` from /opt/nxeon — do NOT touch the live tree or merge into main. Symlink node_modules/.env; never `git add -A` in a worktree.

## Target file

`app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx` — the customer-facing "Shared Hosting" overview/list page. Read it fully first, along with whatever component(s) it renders for the account cards, to understand the current data-fetching and rendering pattern before redesigning.

## Data model (read `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `HostingAccount`/`HostingPlan` models fully — do not fabricate any numbers, wire everything to real fields)

`HostingAccount` has: `primaryDomain`, `status` (enum: PENDING/PROVISIONING/ACTIVE/SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING), `diskQuotaMB` (already includes purchased extra disk), `extraDiskGB`, `maxSites`, `maxDatabases`, `termMonths`, `expiresAt` (renewal date), relation to `plan: HostingPlan` (`name`, `priceCents`, `mailboxes` — -1 means unlimited). Find how CURRENT usage (websites created, databases created, storage actually used, mailboxes created) is tracked — likely `HostingAddonDomain`/`HostingDatabase`/`HostingSubdomain` relation counts and a usage-sync field (grep for "diskUsedMB" or similar, referenced elsewhere this session as filled in by a "hostingUsageSweep" worker job) — use REAL current-usage numbers from these relations/fields, not placeholders.

## The current live page (I'm describing it precisely since I can see it but can't hand you the file directly)

A gradient hero banner card: "COMPUTE" eyebrow label, "Shared Hosting" H1, a description paragraph, a "Deploy new site" button (gradient purple-to-blue pill, arrow icon) top-area, and a decorative teal/cyan gradient background with a large faint globe-outline icon on the right side of the banner. Below that: a "Web Hosting" section heading + short paragraph. Below that: a "YOUR HOSTING ACCOUNTS" label, then a responsive 2-column grid of account cards — each card shows the primary domain (bold, large), a status pill (green dot + "active" lowercase text) top-right, a subtitle line (plan tier name + PHP version, e.g. "Starter · PHP 8.3"), a row of small pill/chip tags (e.g. "Storage 0.11 / 10 GB", "1 extra site", "2 DBs", a green "HTTPS" pill), and a "Manage →" text link at the bottom-left of the card. Whole page is dark navy/violet-cyan themed, matching the rest of the dashboard.

## The target redesign direction (a mockup the owner had generated and approved the general direction of — described precisely, does not need to be pixel-exact, just similar in structure and information density)

Keep the SAME real Nxeon dashboard chrome (sidebar nav, top bar) — only the page content below the header changes. Structure, top to bottom:

1. **Header row**: "Shared Hosting" H1 + subtitle paragraph on the left (keep existing copy style), and on the right a single primary CTA button. **Change its label from "Deploy new site" to "Deploy new hosting"** (gradient purple-blue pill, rocket icon, matches existing button styling elsewhere in the dashboard — check `components/customer/DeployWizard.tsx`'s entry points or similar CTAs for the exact existing button component/style to reuse, don't invent a new button style).

2. **A single wide summary/stat card**, divided into 5 sections in one row (stack responsively on mobile): 
   - "Active Plans" — a server/stack icon, the real COUNT of this customer's active `HostingAccount` rows, with a small green status dot beside the number.
   - "Websites" — globe icon, real `used / total` across all their accounts (sum of maxSites or actual site count vs. real usage), with a thin colored progress bar underneath (purple).
   - "Databases" — database icon, real `used / total`, blue progress bar.
   - "Storage" — a storage/disk icon, real `used GB / total GB` (sum `diskQuotaMB`/1024 for total, real usage for used), cyan/teal progress bar.
   - "Emails" — envelope icon, real `used / total` mailboxes (handle the `-1 = unlimited` case sensibly — don't show "5 / -1", show "5 / Unlimited" or omit the bar for that dimension), orange progress bar.
   Each section's progress bar fill % must be computed from the REAL used/total ratio, clamped 0-100, never fabricated.

3. **Tabs + search row**: "All Plans" / "Active" / "Expired" tabs on the left (client-side filter by `status`, treat SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING/PENDING/PROVISIONING as whatever bucket makes sense — use your judgment and state your mapping in the report), a "Search plans..." text input filtering by domain/plan name on the right, plus a small filter/sliders icon button beside the search (can be a no-op placeholder or wire to something sensible like a plan-tier filter — your call, keep it simple if you don't have a clear extra dimension to filter by).

4. **A table-style list of plan rows** replacing the old 2-column card grid. Each row shows:
   - **Plan column**: a small colored rounded-square icon (globe icon, background color/gradient VARYING BY PLAN TIER — e.g. violet for the cheapest tier, blue for mid, green/teal for a business tier, orange for the top tier — derive a consistent color mapping across whatever real `HostingPlan` tiers exist, check `HostingPlan.slug`/`name`/`sortOrder` to build a sensible tier→color function), then the account's OWN customer-set label if one exists (check if `HostingAccount` has a `label`/`name` field separate from `primaryDomain` — if not, fall back to `primaryDomain` as the display name) in bold, plus **a colored pill/tag beside the name showing the plan tier** (e.g. "Starter", "Pro", "Business", "Enterprise" — whatever this platform's real `HostingPlan` names actually are, don't invent tier names that don't exist), then below that the primary domain as a clickable link with an external-link icon opening in a new tab.
   - **Usage column**: the same 4 mini-stats as the summary card (Websites / Databases / Storage / Emails) but PER-ACCOUNT, each with its own small progress bar, laid out horizontally.
   - **Renewal date column**: a calendar icon + the real `expiresAt` formatted date.
   - **Status column**: a colored dot + status pill (green "Active", appropriate colors for other statuses — check how status is displayed elsewhere in this dashboard, e.g. `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx`, for the established status-color convention and reuse it rather than inventing a new one).
   - **Cost column**: bold price (`plan.priceCents` formatted) + smaller "/ month" (or "/ year" if `termMonths === 12` — handle both correctly, don't hardcode "/month").
   - **A 3-dot vertical action-menu button** (dropdown: Manage, and whatever other actions the OLD page's "Manage →" link led to plus anything else already available elsewhere for a hosting account — check `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx` for what actions genuinely exist before inventing menu items).
   - **The entire row must be clickable** to navigate to the account's detail page (`/dashboard/hosting/[id]`) — but the action-menu button and the domain link must `stopPropagation` so clicking THEM doesn't also trigger the row-level navigation (this is a common gotcha — get it right, test it if you can).

5. **Footer**: "Showing X of Y plans" text + pagination controls if there are more rows than fit one page (check if the old page had any pagination — if account counts are always small in practice, a client-side single-page render with a "Showing X of X" label and no-op pagination controls is fine, don't over-engineer real server-side pagination unless the existing data-fetch pattern already supports it cheaply).

## Constraints

- Match Nxeon's real existing design tokens/components — grep for how status pills, progress bars, and stat cards are ALREADY built elsewhere in this dashboard (e.g. `app/admin/visitors/page.tsx` had progress-bar-style node gauges earlier this session, `components/admin/` has various stat card patterns) and reuse/extend those rather than inventing a parallel design system.
- Do not fabricate any usage numbers — if a real usage-tracking field doesn't exist for one of the 4 dimensions, say so clearly in your report and use the best real proxy available (e.g. count of related rows) rather than a placeholder.
- Do not touch any OTHER dashboard page, the custom-server-plans work, PayPal, Namecheap, or location-pages work — separate agents/workstreams, unrelated files.
- Do not deploy to staging/production — I review and ship.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npm test` — no new failures beyond the current 34 pre-existing baseline (pricing/proration/auth-related, unrelated to this page).
3. Visually verify via a local dev server + screenshot (this repo's past sessions used Playwright for this — check for that pattern) against a real account that has at least one HostingAccount row, if one exists in the dev/staging DB, or describe clearly in your report if you had to verify structurally without real visual confirmation.

## Report format

Design decisions made (tier→color mapping, status-color reuse, pagination approach, action-menu contents), any usage dimension you couldn't wire to real data and what you used instead, files created/modified, verification results (including whether you got a real visual check), worktree path/branch name.

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)

You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.

Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.

Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:explain-usage: Explain where this session's tokens went, with one simple chart in plain language. Use when the user says things like "explain my usage", "where did my tokens go", or asks for a usage breakdown.
- anthropic-skills:import-memory: Import a memory export from another AI assistant into Claude's memory — conversationally, additively, and with the content treated as data.

Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.

This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations as PowerPoint (.pptx) files; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email, summary, or creating a different type of slide deck); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint or .pptx file, or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. However, when the user asks for a deck, slides, a slide deck, or a presentation without naming a file format, default to using a dedicated slide-deck artifact type or a separate slides skill if this session offers one; otherwise, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

Work complete. Summary below.

## What was done

Worktree: `/opt/nxeon-wip-hosting-redesign`, branch `feature/hosting-overview-redesign` (node_modules and .env symlinked from `/opt/nxeon`).

**Files modified:**
- `lib/actions-hosting.ts` — extended `HostingAccountView` + `toView()` + the two query call sites (`listHostingAccounts`, `getHostingAccount`) to select real per-account data that wasn't previously exposed: `_count` on `databases`/`addonDomains`/`subdomains` (real usage), plus `plan.slug`/`sortOrder`/`priceCents`/`mailboxes` and the account's own `termMonths`/`annualDiscountPct`. Added a shared `HOSTING_ACCOUNT_INCLUDE` const so both call sites stay in sync.
- `app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx` — swapped the big `<PortalHero>` banner for a plain `<PageHeader>` row (title/subtitle left, CTA right), matching the target mockup's denser header. CTA label changed to "Deploy new hosting".
- `components/customer/HostingClient.tsx` — full rewrite: summary stat card (5 sections), tabs+search+tier-filter row, table-style plan list, footer with real pagination.

**File created:**
- `components/customer/hosting/OverviewIcons.tsx` — small icon set (stack/globe/db/disk/mail/calendar/external-link/dots/search/sliders), following the exact existing icon convention (24×24, stroke=currentColor, strokeWidth 1.7) from `components/portal/Shell.tsx`; several shapes reused verbatim from there and from `PortalHero`.

A temporary unauthenticated preview route (`app/preview-hosting/page.tsx`) was created for screenshot verification only and deleted afterward — not part of the deliverable.

## Design decisions

- **Tier→color**: real `HostingPlan` tiers are only Starter (sortOrder 0), Business (1), Pro (2) — no "Enterprise" exists. Mapped starter→violet, business→teal, pro→orange, keyed by `plan.slug` with a 4-color ramp fallback by `sortOrder` for any future tier.
- **Status colors**: reused `StatusDot`/the existing `statusColors` map in `components/ui/primitives.tsx` verbatim (already covers ACTIVE/PENDING/PROVISIONING/SUSPENDED/FAILED/DELETING) — no new status-color scheme invented.
- **Tabs bucket mapping**: `HostingAccountStatus` has no literal "expired" state. Traced `worker/product-renewals.ts` and confirmed an unpaid/past-due account is flipped to `SUSPENDED` by the renewal sweep — so "Expired" tab = `status === "SUSPENDED"`. "Active" = `status === "ACTIVE"`. PENDING/PROVISIONING/FAILED/DELETING accounts appear only under "All Plans".
- **Websites/Databases usage semantics**: reused the exact convention already established on the account-detail page (`HostingTabs.tsx`'s "Extra sites" QuotaTile) — used = subdomains+addonDomains created (real `_count`), total = `maxSites` (primary domain isn't counted against the budget, matching that existing tile). Databases: used = real `HostingDatabase` count, total = `maxDatabases`.
- **CTA button**: kept the exact shared `<DeployButton>` component (arrow icon) rather than inventing a rocket-icon variant — that button is reused identically across Servers/Games/Hosting; changing its icon would have touched unrelated out-of-scope pages. Only the label text changed, as explicitly requested.
- **Cost column**: shows the *real charged* amount via `termPriceCents(plan.priceCents, termMonths, annualDiscountPct)` — the same formula the renewal sweep actually bills — rather than always showing the flat `plan.priceCents` mislabeled "/year". Verified against mock data (e.g. $499/mo × 12 × 20% off = $47.90/year, exactly as rendered).
- **Pagination**: implemented as real, functional client-side pagination (10/page) since all accounts are already fetched in one query; the footer/controls fully hide themselves when everything fits one page (verified: "Showing 1–5 of 5 plans" with no controls in the test data).
- **Action menu**: Manage, Visit site (ACTIVE only), Check now/Go live (calls the real `recheckHostingHealth`, ACTIVE only), Retry setup (calls real `retryHostingProvision`, FAILED only), Cancel account (deep-links to `?tab=settings`, where the real two-step-confirm cancel flow already lives — not reimplemented inline, since that's a destructive, domain-typed-confirmation action).

## Usage dimension that could not be wired to real data

**Mailboxes ("used" count)**: traced the whole schema — `Mailbox` only relates to `EmailSubscription` (the separate "Business Email" product), never to `HostingAccount`. There is no `HostingMailbox`-equivalent model anywhere, so shared-hosting mailbox *usage* is genuinely untracked in this codebase (confirmed by grepping every "mailbox" reference in `prisma/schema.prisma`). I did not fabricate a used count: the UI shows only the real included total (`plan.mailboxes`, handling `-1` → "Unlimited"), a "N incl." label instead of a fraction, and no progress bar for that dimension, with a visible note ("Mailbox usage isn't tracked for shared hosting yet").

**Storage**: real, but nullable until the `hostingUsageSweep` worker measures a new account (`diskUsedMB`/`usageAt`). Handled by showing "not measured yet" per-row and a "some accounts are still measuring usage" note on the summary card when any ACTIVE account has a null value, rather than showing a fabricated 0.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (0 errors), both before and after changes.
2. `npm test` — 1191 pass / 34 fail, identical to the pre-existing baseline confirmed before any edits (same 34 pricing/proration/auth failures, unrelated to this page).
3. **Real visual verification**: ran `next dev` in the worktree on an isolated port (3919) and screenshotted the actual, unmodified `HostingClient` component against fabricated `HostingAccountView` rows (5 accounts spanning ACTIVE/PROVISIONING/SUSPENDED/FAILED and all 3 tiers) via Playwright — desktop (1440px) and mobile (420px) full-page screenshots, plus interactive checks: the "Expired" tab correctly isolated the one SUSPENDED account, the 3-dot menu opened with the right contextual items without triggering row navigation, and a click on empty row space correctly `router.push`'d to `/dashboard/hosting/acc_business` while the domain link and menu button's `stopPropagation` worked as required. This used a temporary unauthenticated preview route (deleted after use) rather than the live `/dashboard/hosting` route, since that route requires a real customer session and this worktree's `.env` points at the live production database — no writes, logins, or mutating actions were performed against it.

Note: mid-verification I ran a broad `pkill -9 -f "next-server\|next dev"` intending to stop only my own port-3919 dev server; it matched pattern text shared with the live `nxeon-web` systemd service's process name. I immediately checked — `systemctl status nxeon-web` showed it had been running continuously since well before that command (no restart), so production was not affected — but the command was too broad and I should have scoped it by PID/port instead. Flagging this so you're aware, even though no harm resulted.
